title: Who Climbs With You: Guides, Porters and Cooks on Kilimanjaro
excerpt: You never climb Kilimanjaro alone. Meet the crew: lead guide, assistant guides, cook, waiter and porters, and what each of them does.
body:
A Kilimanjaro climb is a team effort. Behind every climber is a crew that carries, cooks, guides and looks after you.

## Lead guide

The lead guide is responsible for the group: route, pace, daily health checks and decisions about safety. Guides are licensed by Kilimanjaro National Park and trained in first aid. Read about [how mountain guides are trained](/blog/mountain-guide-certification/).

## Assistant guides

On larger groups, assistant guides walk with climbers at different paces, so nobody is rushed. On summit night there is usually one guide for every one or two climbers.

## Cook

The cook prepares three meals a day plus snacks, often with fresh ingredients carried up. Read [what you eat on Kilimanjaro](/blog/kilimanjaro-food-on-the-mountain/).

## Waiter or camp crew

They serve meals, bring hot water for washing in the morning and set up the mess tent.

## Porters

Porters carry tents, food, water and your main bag. Park rules set a maximum load per porter. Porters walk ahead and set up camp before you arrive.

## How big is the crew?

For two climbers on an eight-day route, a crew of ten or more is normal. It sounds like a lot, but everything you need for a week on the mountain has to be carried.

## Fair treatment

Fair wages, good meals, proper equipment and reasonable loads are essential. See [porter welfare on Kilimanjaro](/blog/kilimanjaro-porter-welfare/).

## At the end

On the last day there is often a small ceremony with songs, and the moment to thank the crew. Read [how tipping works](/blog/kilimanjaro-tipping-guide-crew/).
